REPORT: Flávio Bolsonaro Flees Brazil After Election Loss

Wild chain of events

Actual Article Body:
(Photo by Ton Molina/Getty Images)

Brazilian presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro fled his country Tuesday for the U.S. after losing a keenly contested presidential election to incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, according to multiple reports.

Bolsonaro and his family would receive U.S. visas, a U.S. State Department official who requested anonymity told outlets hours before Bolsonaro’s reported arrival in the U.S. The official, however, did not confirm whether Bolsonaro had left Brazil or whether his family was on the way to the U.S., according to The Associated Press.

Lula could not confirm Bolsonaro’s location and said that Bolsonaro left Brazil in the wake of his loss Sunday in the runoff election.

Bolsonaro left Brazil under a cloud as the Brazilian Supreme Court had asked him Monday to hand over his passports over money laundering allegations and then canceled the passports as he missed the deadline, the BBC reported. The court demanded his passports after he visited his father, former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro, who is under house arrest. The younger Bolsonaro, who is also an Italian citizen, had agreed to comply with the order but arrived in the U.S. hours after his passports were canceled, The New York Times reported. (RELATED: All Bets Are Off On Brazil’s Presidential Election, Literally)

Brazilian authorities are investigating Bolsonaro’s potential connection to a Brazilian lawyer who is alleged to have laundered over $1 billion through an online gambling and trading scheme. Officials also want to look into allegations he received millions of dollars from a jailed banker at the heart of a multimillion-dollar financial fraud scandal, according to The New York Times.

Bolsonaro reportedly raised the millions to finance a documentary of his father.

Lula had defeated the elder Bolsonaro in the 2022 presidential election, after which the latter went on to bag a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup against Lula, according to The Associated Press.

The elder Bolsonaro also fled Brazil for the U.S. state of Florida following his election loss to Lula, but returned to Brazil after three months and became enmeshed in investigations and court trials. He also hid in the Hungarian embassy in Brazil for two days and intended to obtain asylum in Argentina, according to The New York Times.

The younger Bolsonaro has a brother in Texas and the Bolsonaro family have a relationship with U.S. President Donald Trump, according to The Associated Press.

While Trump did not offer official endorsement to the younger Bolsonaro during the 2026 election, the State Department worked covertly to enhance his chances, The New York Times reported.

Vocal critics of the elder Jair Bolsonaro, like liberal journalist Glenn Greenwald, have accused leftist movements in both Brazil and America of wrongly venerating the Supreme Court judge who went after Flávio Bolsonaro.

“Then — starting in 2019 — Moraes began censoring, imprisoning and persecuting Lula’s enemies and imprisoning his own critics, and was overnight transformed by the large Brazilian media and the left into the Savior of Brazilian Justice and Democracy,” Greenwald, who actively covers Brazilian politics, wrote Oct. 27. “Only on the left can one transform from from *fascist and genocidal racist* to heroic guardian of justice in less than a decade.”

Stated Claim / Post Context:
Brazil’s Flavio Bolsonaro arrives in Miami as Trump approves his refuge in US

President Trump expressed support for defeated Brazilian Presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro coming to the US after his shocking loss, as he faces an investigation back home.

Actual Article Body:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

WASHINGTON — Defeated Brazilian Presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro touched down in Miami, Florida, Wednesday with his family after fleeing his country in the wake of his shocking loss.

Flavio’s arrival comes as President Trump has expressed support for him to take refuge in the US after controversial Vice-President of the Supreme Federal Court of Brazil Alexandre de Moraes ordered him to surrender his passport

“Well, I would approve,” Trump told reporters late Tuesday of Flavio taking refuge in the US. “The election was very strange, and I thought it was terrible.”

“I didn’t take sides. I know them both. I know [Brazilian President Luiz Inácio] Lula [da Silva], I know Flavio a little bit,” the president added. “But I wasn’t involved.”

The Post previously reported that Flavio and his family are expected to receive visas from the State Department. Flavio had departed Brazil with his wife and two daughters.

Trump had been chummy with Flavio’s father, former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro, who was defeated by Lula in 2022. Flavio’s brother Eduardo had already been living in the US prior to his arrival.

Flavio, a senator in Brazil, had won the first round of voting in Brazil earlier this month, but the 81-year-old Lula staged a dramatic comeback in the runoffs on Sunday.

The election faced controversy. Both Flavio and Lula had petitioned for a nationwide extension of voting due to concerns about transportation issues causing interruptions.

Brazilian Supreme Court Judge Cristiano Zanin, who previously served as Lula’s attorney, greenlit a national two-hour extension of voting, though there were questions about how evenly that went into effect.

Lula’s victory defied international trends against incumbents and a regional trend of South American countries shifting to the right. His victory was also commanding.

Lula garnered over 64 million votes, while the Bolsonaro scion got fewer than 60 million, marking a roughly 4 percentage point margin of victory.

Flavio hasn’t been charged with anything and has claimed that the investigation into him is political persecution. The probe is believed to revolve around corruption concerns, money laundering, and ties to other scandals that have rocked Brazilian politics.

Moraes, a highly controversial figure on Brazil’s Supreme Court, issued the order to seize his passports in apparent response to Flavio suggesting on a podcast that he’d flee if he lost the election.

The Brazilian Supreme Court judge has been very aggressive in cracking down on right-wing figures, igniting censorship concerns, and is facing his own corruption-related questions.

Lula previously served jail time from 2018 through 2019 over corruption charges, but Brazil’s Supreme Court later annulled it so that he could run for reelection. Jair is serving out a 27-year prison sentence related to a coup attempt after his 2022 defeat.

Trump had been famously chummy with Jair, who was generally considered more pro-America in his foreign policy approach than Lula.

Breaking: Flavio Bolsonaro arrives in Miami after fleeing Brazil

The presidential contender disappeared days after losing the election, prompting intense speculation he had left Brazil for the US.

By Thomas Morgan

Topic:World Politics

Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro was seen disembarking from a plane in Florida on Thursday morning, local time. (Reuters: Eva Marie Uzcategui)

Flavio Bolsonaro has arrived in the United States, less than a week after losing Brazil's presidential election.

Mr Bolsonaro, who is the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, had been facing a number of legal battles in Brazil and had been ordered by a court to surrender his passport earlier this week.

But the senator instead disappeared, prompting intense speculation that he had fled to the United States.

Mr Bolsonaro, who loses his immunity from prosecution when his Senate term ends in February, had said on Monday after the order to hand in his passports that he had no plans to ​flee.

"I have never thought about leaving the country," he said.

"I will hand over my passports and defend myself against this travesty, which ​is a clear attempt ⁠to intimidate me."

Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro could be seen being escorted out of Opa-locka Executive Airport, shielded by umbrellas. (Reuters: Eva Marie Uzcategui)

Mr Bolsonaro, who ran on a populist platform, was widely expected to win Sunday's election but suffered a shock defeat to leftist incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva.

In pictures published on Thursday, Mr Bolsonaro can be seen disembarking a plane at Opa-locka Executive Airport near Miami, Florida.

It is believed the US government will grant them entry visas, in a move that is likely to deepen the rift between the US and Brazil, two of the Americas' most populous countries.

US President Donald Trump told reporters earlier this week that he would approve of Mr Bolsonaro coming to the United States, after his State Department said it would give them entry visas.

Mr Lula has accused Washington of colluding with the Bolsonaro family to help return them to power.

Mr Bolsonaro's father, Jair Bolsonaro, also fled to Florida after losing the 2022 presidential election to Mr Lula before returning to Brazil three months later.

Flavio Bolsonaro, an incumbent senator for Rio de Janeiro, is under investigation by Brazil’s Supreme Court for alleged corruption, money laundering and tax evasion in two cases.

The court had ordered Mr Bolsonaro to hand over his regular and diplomatic passports by noon Tuesday, just two days after he lost the vote to Mr Lula.

It remained unclear whether he had complied, but allies said he also had an Italian passport.
